title: Hundreds of migrants cross Channel in one day after 10-day lull
summary:
Tap the questions belowHow many people cross the English Channel in small boats?
Between 1 January and 27 August 2026, a total of 16,391 people crossed the English Channel by small boat from France.
Nearly all those who arrive by small boat claim asylum.
Small boat arrivals made up 40% of asylum applications between July 2025 to June 2026.
At least 84 people died while attempting to cross the Channel in 2024, according to the United Nations (UN).

title: Trump administration deports relative of Afghans who helped US military to Central African Republic
summary:
DAKAR, Senegal (AP) — The United States on Saturday deported dozens of people to the Central African Republic, including an Afghan whose brothers collaborated with the U.S. military, his lawyer and an advocacy group said.
Another one of his brothers was a pilot trained by the U.S. and was killed by the Taliban, she added.
The deportation flight which landed in Central African Republic's capital Bangui on Saturday, included 12 Afghans and eight Iranians, as well as several people from Nepal and Nicaragua, said Savi Arvey, director of policy, refugee and immigrant rights at Human Rights First.
Immigration lawyers say the practice is being used as a legal loophole to indirectly return some asylum seekers to countries they fled.
The flight on Saturday is the second to the Central African Republic since June, which carried two dozen migrants, including an Iranian woman facing persecution in her home country.

title: Malaysia to return 1,500 Rohingya refugees next month, despite safety fears
summary:
Share Malaysia to return 1,500 Rohingya refugees next month, despite safety fears on social mediaMalaysia has finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will see at least 1,500 eligible Myanmar refugees return home on September 29, the government said.
“The repatriation process will use two Myanmar naval warships and a hospital ship,” according to a Malaysia Home Ministry statement.
There were 10,388 Myanmar nationals held at immigration detention depots by mid-August, the ministry said, with not all considered refugees.
Rights groups raise safety concernsEarlier this month, the government said it would not proceed with the repatriation if the refugees’ lives would be at risk upon return.
“Malaysia, as a responsible country, will not return the 5,000 Myanmar refugees if they would either be persecuted or their lives would be threatened,” Fahmi Fadzil, the Malaysian communications minister, said.
